result:
Solution 1 is correct. In $K^q_{\lceil n/2\rceil,\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, every triangle contains exactly one matching edge $u_iv_i$ and one vertex $w$ of the other part. Two triangles can share exactly one vertex only if they use different matching edges and the same $w$, so bowties are centered only in the part of size $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Each such center gives $\binom{q}{2}$ bowties, for a total of $\lfloor n/2\rfloor\binom{q}{2}$.

Solutions 2 and 3 both assume that splitting the $q$ edges between the two parts keeps the spectral radius the same. That holds only to first order. The second-order terms depend on how the added edges interact, so the split graph need not satisfy $\lambda(G)\ge\lambda(K^q)$. Their claimed value $\approx nq^2/8$ therefore rests on an unjustified step. Solution 1 also matches the expected form of this result, a spectral Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau-type bound attained by $K^q$, though I did not verify the extremality claim independently.

CHOICE: 1
